apps/desktop/electron/services/ipc-route.content:
The IPC trust boundary is fail-open and prefix-based, so it can be spoofed.

1) Fail-open: `event.senderFrame` is `null` for destroyed/unknown frames (and nullable in Electron), and an empty URL makes this return `true`, granting access to the privileged channels (`config/set`, `config/import`, `master/*`, `show/*`) instead of denying.
2) Prefix match: `startsWith("http://localhost:5173")` also matches `http://localhost:5173@evil.com/…` (the string after `@` is the real host) and `http://localhost:5173.evil.com`, letting a spoofed frame pass the allowlist. `file://` likewise accepts any local file origin.

Compare the parsed exact origin instead and fail closed when the frame is unknown. Note the same prefix pattern also lives in `main.ts` (allowedNavigation/onBeforeRequest), so the string should be a single shared constant rather than a hardcoded literal here.

Request validation, handler execution, and response validation all share one `try`/`catch`, so every failure collapses into the same `E_HANDLER` code at the bottom of `dispatch`. Consequences:

- A malformed/absent request payload (a renderer bug) is reported as an `E_HANDLER` server fault, making client/server faults indistinguishable in status and in the audit log.
- A response that violates the channel's response schema (a real protocol/handler bug) is reported identically to a thrown handler error, hiding response-schema mismatches.
- The response is validated *after* the handler's side effect has already run. If a handler mutates state (e.g. `setMasterBlackout`) but returns a shape the response schema rejects, the router returns `{ ok: false }` even though the action applied, so the renderer may retry/report a false failure.

Use distinct error codes (e.g. `E_REQUEST` for `request.parse`, `E_HANDLER` for handler throws, `E_RESPONSE` for `response.parse`) and audit them separately so protocol mismatches surface in the UI/status.

A track that is currently being analyzed but has no model yet falls into the `!model` branch and is reported as `NEEDS ANALYSIS`, so consumers (e.g. `features/live/live.ts` line 68) show the wrong readiness during analysis. The sibling helper `libraryTrackRow` in `routes/library/library-rows.ts` handles this with an explicit `analyzing` flag. Add an `analyzing` parameter and return `ANALYZING` for the not-yet-modeled case.

Also the comment claims waveform/PSSI/stems/cues lanes that this function never returns. Use `b.index` (or `b.bpm`) for beat alignment and align the comment with what is actually produced.

The `!model` branch returns `trackId: ""`. Callers typically use `trackId` as a React key or lookup id (see `routes/library/track-key.ts` `libraryRowKey` / `isSelectedTrack`), so multiple placeholder rows will all collapse to the same empty key and selection state can bleed across them. Return `null` for the id (and let the caller supply a stable placeholder) or document that empty ids must not be used as keys.

No test in this file ever calls `connection.write()` or exercises the notify path, so notification dispatch, write/notify plumbing and timeout handling could all be broken while every assertion still passes. Add a test that drives `subscribe`/`write` and asserts the frame bytes, and have the fake surface (or honour) the timeout so timeout behavior is at least observable.

This test asserts only the summary/report reason strings after the toolkit load failure — it never performs a `scan()` or `connect()` on the resulting selector. Because `createBackendSelector` makes noble the primary with `secondary: null` in this branch, a regression that sets the reason correctly but leaves noble unusable (e.g. broken connect/scan) would still pass. Add an assertion that `connect()`/`scan()` actually succeeds on the noble fallback.

packages/ble/src/backends.test.ts.content: The per-device override is only exercised with a single `connect("BAD:01")`. The test never connects to the same failing device again, so it does not verify that the override record (a) persists across calls and (b) prevents re-attempting the failing toolkit backend. A bug where `noteFallback` is not consulted on repeat connects, or where the override resets, would go undetected. Add a second `connect("BAD:01")` and assert it still returns a noble connection and that the toolkit adapter's `seen` does not gain a second entry.

This test constructs `BackendSelector` directly using the internal `SelectorDeps` shape (`primary`/`primaryKind`/`primaryReason`/`secondary`) instead of going through `createBackendSelector`. This bypasses the production wiring and won't detect drift if the factory changes what it passes. It also never asserts the 'retries once' contract: it does not verify the primary was tried first, nor that the retry happens exactly once (no loop). Build the selector via `createBackendSelector` with a `scanFails` toolkit adapter and assert the primary's call count / that the retry succeeded.

The LatestWinsChannel coverage only checks synchronous burst behaviour (depth/dropped/take after three back-to-back sends). Interleaved send/take ordering is never tested, so a queuing implementation or a `take()` that returns a stale frame could still pass. Add a send→take→send sequence (and assert `dropped` does not increment when `take()` empties the slot) to pin down the exact latest-wins/drop semantics.
